newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's banking chief demands proof of laundering.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's banking chief demands proof of laundering.

text.p: The head of the Mexican Bankers Association on Friday demanded proof of drug money laundering in Mexico after a U.S. Congressman said drug profits in Mexico may reach up to $30 billion a year.
"We continue to say that let's hope they give us proof so that we can attack," Jose Madariaga told reporters after a meeting with Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar.

He was responding to estimates quoted by Spencer Bachus, an Alabama Republican who heads the oversight and investigations subcomittee of the House Banking Committee, that from $6 billion to $30 billion is earned in the Mexican drugs trade each year.
Bachus said there were no safeguards against money laundering in Mexico comparable with those in the United States.
"Once drug profits are in Mexican banks, the cartels are free to spend the money anywhere," Bachus said.
Madariaga said Mexican banks were currently not facing any investigation by local authorities into suspected money laundering.
